Good Orange County website design begins with a fact every local already knows: nobody lives in "Orange County" the way they live in a city. They live in Anaheim, Tustin, Laguna Niguel or Yorba Linda, and that is the word they type when they need a plumber or a dentist. Dominion Web Design Pro writes sites that use those real names, prints its prices, and builds a free demo before anyone talks about payment.

Maurice Johnson writes every page himself from Big Sandy, Texas. What follows is how we would think through a site for an Orange County business, especially one that works inside homeowners associations.

Orange County website design starts with the city on the search bar

The county has 34 incorporated cities and roughly 3.15 million residents, according to the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate. Santa Ana is the county seat, and Anaheim, Santa Ana and Irvine are the three largest cities. There is no single downtown that everyone drives to. Instead, the county is a patchwork of city centers, beach towns, business parks and planned communities, each with its own name and its own reputation.

That shapes how web design in Orange County should be done. A pool service based in Huntington Beach that also works Fountain Valley and Costa Mesa has three places customers search by name. A dental office in Fullerton might draw patients from Fullerton, Brea and Placentia. A one-page site that says "serving all of Orange County" asks Google to guess. A site with a short, true page about each city you actually serve gives it something to match.

  • North CountyAnaheim, Fullerton, Buena Park, Brea, Yorba Linda, Placentia, La Habra
  • Central CountySanta Ana, Orange, Tustin, Irvine, Garden Grove, Westminster
  • CoastHuntington Beach, Newport Beach, Costa Mesa, Laguna Beach, Dana Point, San Clemente
  • South CountyLake Forest, Mission Viejo, Laguna Niguel, Rancho Santa Margarita, and unincorporated Ladera Ranch

Those groupings are informal, and locals argue about where the lines fall. That is fine. The point is to use the names your customers use.

Planned communities, HOAs and the home-service website

A large share of Orange County was built as master-planned communities, and that changes how home-service businesses sell. Irvine grew from a plan drawn up by the architect William Pereira around 1960, which called for residential villages, each with its own boundaries, a school, a park and a shopping center. Woodbridge, one of the early villages, holds about 9,600 homes on 2.7 square miles. To the south, the O'Neill family and partners formed the Mission Viejo Company in 1963 to build Mission Viejo. A later family company planned the city of Rancho Santa Margarita, and a successor company planned Ladera Ranch, which is still unincorporated county land.

Many of these neighborhoods have homeowners associations, and an exterior project there commonly needs the association's architectural approval, which is a separate step from any city permit, before work begins. Roofers, painters, landscapers, fence and solar installers all live with this.

What an HOA-friendly contractor site explains

  1. Who files the applicationWhether you prepare the HOA paperwork, help the homeowner prepare it, or leave it to them.
  2. What the board will want to seeDrawings, product names, color and material samples, and any neighbor notice the community requires.
  3. How approval and permit fit togetherWhich comes first in the cities you work, and how both affect your start date.
  4. When you can scheduleA plain note that the calendar starts once approval is in hand, so nobody is surprised.

Homeowners researching a project in Ladera Ranch or Woodbridge are already thinking about their HOA. A contractor whose site answers those questions sounds like someone who has done it, and that is often what earns the call. We write those pages from your real process, not from assumptions.

Your license number belongs on the website

California treats a contractor website as advertising. The Contractors State License Board says the license number must appear in advertising under Business and Professions Code section 7030.5, and its 2020 bulletin names online postings and websites along with newspaper, radio and TV ads. CSLB lists civil penalties for violations.

On every contractor site we build for California, the license number sits in the footer of every page and on the contact page, exactly as you give it to us. Homeowners can look a number up on the CSLB site, and a number that is easy to find saves them the trouble of asking. This is a building practice, not legal advice: you confirm the number and any other required wording before launch.

An Orange County web design company, or one builder?

Search for an Orange County web design company and you will find studios in Irvine business parks and agencies in Costa Mesa with design teams, account managers and video crews. If you want branding work, a photo shoot at your location and regular meetings, one of those website design companies in Orange County is the right kind of hire, and a good web design company in Orange County will put its price in writing before you sign.

Orange County website designers who work alone, like us, sell something narrower: one person who writes and builds every page, prices you can read today, and a demo you see before you commit. For a dental practice in Tustin or a CPA in Lake Forest, that usually covers what matters: clear services, the insurance or client types you accept, office hours, a form that emails you, and a page that loads quickly on a phone.

Our packages are paid once. Starter is $497 for five pages and goes live in 7 to 14 days. Pro is $997 for ten pages, a photo gallery, local SEO setup including your Google Business Profile, and ten city pages; its AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month. Agency is $1,997, starting with keyword research across your service area and adding a page for every town and service pair worth having, delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks. It includes setup of an AI phone agent that is free for 7 days and then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time, billed apart from the one-time price. Hosting, maintenance and updates come included while you keep the AI agent, or cost $49 a month without it. We do not sell page counts: a strong page for each city you really serve beats dozens of thin ones.

Web design Orange County, California searches in more than one language

Census QuickFacts reports that 46.4% of Orange County residents age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home (2020 to 2024 estimates). Spanish is part of that, and so is Vietnamese. Little Saigon, centered on Bolsa Avenue in Westminster and reaching into Garden Grove, is described in a California Assembly resolution as the largest Vietnamese community outside Vietnam. Its first Vietnamese-owned businesses opened on Bolsa in the late 1970s.

A pho restaurant, a nail salon or an insurance agency there may have customers who search in Vietnamese first. One well-made page in that language, with services, hours and the phone number, written or checked by someone fluent, can do more than a whole translated site.

Web design Orange County CA homeowners find on a phone

Google's own help page says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. When someone in Rancho Santa Margarita searches "house painter near me," distance is measured from where they stand; when they search "house painter Mission Viejo," it is measured from the town they typed. Either way, a site and a Google Business Profile that name your cities clearly give the matching something to work with. No one can promise a position in those results, and we will not.

Phones carry a large share of those searches, so responsive web design for Orange County customers is the default on every site we build, not an upgrade. The call button, hours, service list and the cities you cover sit at the top on a small screen, and the contact form works with a thumb.

No-cost help for Orange County owners

  • Orange County Inland Empire SBDC Network. Hosted by Cal State Fullerton since 2003, it offers no-cost consulting and training to businesses in Orange, Riverside and San Bernardino counties.
  • SCORE Orange County. Free, confidential mentoring from volunteer business owners, in person, by email or by video, plus workshops, many of them free.
  • Your city's chamber of commerce. In a county of 34 cities, the chamber closest to your customers is usually the one in the city where you work most.

Common questions

How much does Orange County website design cost for a small business?

Local quotes vary from a few hundred dollars to well into five figures, and plenty of firms only quote after a meeting. We print ours. Starter is $497 for five hand-written pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for keyword research and a page for each town and service worth targeting, all paid one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

What should a contractor website in an HOA neighborhood say?

Say plainly who handles the homeowners association paperwork, what the homeowner needs to gather (plans, material samples, color chips), and how HOA review fits with the city permit and your start date. Homeowners in planned communities often expect a wait for approval, and a contractor who explains it up front sounds like one who has done it before. We write that page from your actual process, never from guesses.

Are you an Orange County website design company with an office here, or remote website designers?

No. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson in Big Sandy, Texas, and every Orange County site is built remotely by phone, email and shared links. If you want someone who can stop by your shop in Costa Mesa, a local firm is the better choice. If you want the person who writes your pages to answer your questions directly, the free demo shows you how we work.

Can my website have a Vietnamese or Spanish version?

Yes. We build the extra pages with their own titles so search engines can show them to people searching in that language, and keep your phone number, address and hours identical across versions. The wording in Vietnamese, Spanish or any other language is written or checked by you or a fluent person you trust; we do not publish machine translation as finished copy.

Is responsive web design included for Orange County businesses?

Every package works on phones, tablets and desktop computers. That is not an extra. Most people who find a roofer or a dentist do it on a phone between other things, so the call button, the hours and the address come first on a small screen.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
